title: Cascading tool adapter: streamed result merge & recursion throttling
creator: Sofia Ramirez
description:
Motivation: Multi-tool chains are increasingly common for Redwood customers who mix model function-calls, external tool invocations, and internal helpers (embeddings/rerank). Existing orchestrators either buffer full tool outputs before returning to the caller or allow unbounded injection that creates feedback loops and unmanageable latency/cost. This ticket defines a cascading tool adapter that: 1) streams partial tool outputs back to the caller when safe, 2) incrementally merges tool results into a structured canonical output, and 3) applies recursion/throttle policies to break loops and limit runaway re-invocation.

Scope and goals: Implement a compatibility adapter in the runtime invocation layer that works across hosted/dedicated/private deployments and integrates with the streaming API, function/tool calling contract, and structured-output schema enforcement. The adapter should: (a) add an idempotency and hop-count envelope to tool invocations, (b) support incremental merge semantics for structured outputs (JSON-LD or schema-path-based anchoring), (c) expose backpressure-aware streaming so upstream can consume early tokens without violating SLOs, and (d) enforce a recursion policy with soft and hard limits plus fallbacks to a safe model variant.

Design notes:
- Envelope: each tool invocation attaches metadata: invocation_id, parent_chain (short array of invocation_ids), hop_count, idempotency_key, and compatibility_tags. These are opaque strings to the tool but used by the adapter. Hop_count increments on each tool->tool invocation; if hop_count >= configured_hop_limit trigger soft-stop.
- Streaming merge: the adapter exposes a merge strategy that supports three modes: stream-append (emit as tokens arrive), schema-merge (incrementally populate fields in a canonical JSON response), and pinned-merge (only expose final merged field when stable). A per-route config decides the default.
- Loop/recursion controls:
  * Soft throttle: when hop_count near limit, inject a single-token sentinel into stream that indicates "throttle-warning" to model/runtime and reduce temperature or switch to a smaller model.
  * Hard stop: when hop_count exceeds hard_limit, abort invocation and return structured error with reconciliation hints and candidate fallback result (best-effort cached response).
  * Recursion detection: detect repeated invocation_id patterns or identical idempotency_key reuse beyond threshold and treat as loop.
- Compatibility layer: adapter translates older function-calling shapes into the new envelope (backwards compatible). For example, previous tool outputs that returned raw string results are wrapped into {"_raw": "...", "_format": "legacy-string"} so downstream merge logic can handle them.
- Telemetry: emit events for hop_count, sentinel injections, merge mode chosen, merge conflicts, and fallback triggers. Include sampled traces for expensive loops.

Implementation plan:
1) API shim (small PR): add envelope fields to internal invocation proto and a translation layer for legacy clients.
2) Adapter core: implement hop_count logic, idempotency_key checks, and recursion detector. Unit tests for detection heuristics.
3) Streaming merge engine: build incremental schema-merge that accepts partial JSON fragments and reconciles conflicts (last-writer-wins with conflict metadata). Add stream-append and pinned-merge implementations.
4) Backpressure integration: wire adapter into serving runtime's async queue to avoid queue build-up; apply dynamic batching adjustments when streaming enabled.
5) Rollout and feature flags: default to disabled; enable for specific internal routes first (embeddings-augmented search, chat-toolchains).

Acceptance criteria: 
- End-to-end test: a scripted multi-tool chain (model -> toolA -> toolB -> model) where toolB streams partial JSON and adapter merges into canonical response within SLO.
- Loop protection: simulated loop causes soft-warning at configurable threshold and hard-stop with structured error above hard limit.
- Backwards compatibility: legacy clients that don't send envelope fields still succeed and get legacy-wrapped responses.
- Telemetry: hop_count and fallback events visible in Console within 24 hours.

Out-of-scope: autoscaling policies for Dedicated pools (separate ticket), deep semantic merge (we implement only field-level reconciliation and conflict metadata), UIs for console (separate PM/design ticket).
acceptance_criteria: Scripted multi-tool chain merges partial streamed outputs into canonical JSON without buffering whole-tool outputs
Recursion detection triggers soft-warning and reduces model capacity before hard-stop at configured limit
Legacy clients receive wrapped responses and behavior is unchanged for non-streaming routes
Telemetry events for hop_count, sentinel_injection, merge_conflict, and fallback are visible in runtime traces and Console
implementation_notes:
Edge cases: ensure idempotency_key collision across tenants is namespaced; use tenant_id+key for checks. Use LRU windowed cache for recent invocation_ids (size configurable) to bound memory. For schema-merge, only accept fragments that validate against route schema; invalid fragments produce a merge_conflict event and do not overwrite existing field. Use incremental JSON patch (RFC 6902 style) representation for merges to keep stream small. Backpressure: when consumer is slow, switch adapter to pinned-merge to avoid unbounded partial emissions.

Testing: unit tests for hop_count logic, property-based tests for merge ordering, integration tests with streaming client SDK, load test to measure SLO impact when streaming enabled.

Rollout: feature-flagged via runtime config. Canary on dev -> staging -> 10% hosted -> 100% hosted. Document known risk: increased CPU for merge logic and memory for invocation cache; monitor and add autoscaling rules if necessary.
